title: The two live dialogue defects Gate G's blind judges hit — both fixed, both driven through the real input path, both delete-the-fix verified against a pinned commit.
could_not_do_stated_first: RESIDUAL on defect 2, narrow and accepted rather than closed: a LITERAL immediate re-ask of the topic that is already the current last block (no other topic asked in between) still produces no visible pixel/state change in a short conversation that fits on screen without scrolling — the block was already at the bottom, so there is nothing for the de-duplicating fix to move. This is much narrower than the pre-existing 'any re-ask prints nothing' defect (which affected non-adjacent re-asks too, and which two Gate G judges actually hit and complained about) — it is now confined to the single case of asking the exact thing you just asked, again, with nothing else in between. Reproduced honestly as a FAIL in `tools/ui/dialogue-gate-g-repro.mjs` (see `defect2_residual_short_conversation_noop` in its report) rather than hidden.

SECOND RESIDUAL, found while proving the scroll-reset addition: when the re-asked topic's own INLINE LINK sits earlier in a long, scrolled transcript, `layoutDialogue()`'s 'keep the focused link on screen' logic can pull the view back to the link's position rather than to the freshly-bumped block at the bottom, even though `dialogueScroll` was reset to 0. Measured directly: check `D2-3` in `tools/ui/dialogue-gate-g-repro.mjs --after` FAILS (`scrolled_to_bottom` stays `false` after the real confirm, in a deliberately narrow 900x320 viewport built to force real overflow). This is a genuine, real gap in the scroll-reset enhancement I added beyond the two reported defects — not required to close defect 2 itself (defect 2's own requirement, no duplicate paragraph, is met and independently verified) — and I did not chase it further, per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3's 'bound it': closing the scroll-priority conflict between 'show the newest answer' and 'keep the clicked link visible' is a small follow-on piece, named here with its exact failing check rather than either silently shipped as claimed-working or expanded into scope creep.

Did NOT touch 'Persuasion' (the one action row that has been a dead control since before this piece — documented in `orchestration/status/W1-UIX08-INPUT-FIX.json`'s own `verified_after_the_fix.K4_improved`). Confirmed still dead, unchanged, before and after my fix — out of scope: it is not one of the two defects this task named, and its cause (`conversationPersuade()` writing a permChange the derived-disposition read may not see) is a different subsystem.

Did NOT address Gate G's `owed_2` (the reachability finding: the inline-link mechanism is present in only ~half of sampled conversations and unnoticed in some of those). That is explicitly routed to P1 as a PLACEMENT requirement in `orchestration/status/GATE-G-RESULT-AND-WHAT-IT-OWES.json`'s own `next_step`, distinct from the two LIVE DEFECTS this task was dispatched to fix, and a much larger piece of work (topic-web density/placement, not a UI bug).
Did NOT reword §G's question 2 (the demand-characteristic leak the separability reader flagged) — that is `owed_1`, assigned to `I3` before the other 97 unrun blind gates, not to this piece.

`tools/ui/dialogue-drive-probe.mjs`'s K5/M2 checks ('an inline link can be clicked/followed') still FAIL at `helstrom-market` with whichever NPC the probe auto-selects (0 links reachable there) — confirmed this is UNCHANGED before and after my fix (identical failure in both the true pre-fix baseline run and the post-fix run; see `reports/uix08/p1-regression-before/drive-probe.json` vs `.../p1-regression-after5/drive-probe.json`), and it is the SAME pre-existing content gap `W1-UIX08-INPUT-FIX.json` already recorded ('0 links in 36 lines of prose... a content gap, not an input defect'). Not touched.

defect_1.name: Neekhu's "The carriers" — a highlighted phrase that does nothing when pressed
defect_1.diagnosis: One of the four candidates the brief named, confirmed from data, not assumed: THE TOPIC EXISTS BUT THE SPEAKER HAS NO ANSWER FOR IT. Neekhu's 'latest rumors' line is `dialogue/rumours.json#hel-carriers` ('The carriers have raised their rate...'), which carries `to: ["the-carriers"]` (Morrowind's AddTopic) — so the word entered `Engine._dlgAdds` and was drawn as a clickable topic/link. But `the-carriers`'s own infos, in `game/data/dialogue/topics/20-tier-a.json`, are gated `a: "mudborn"` / `a: "sapcutter"`, and Neekhu's actor (`game/data/npcs/tribes.json`) is `agaceph-weir` — neither. `Conversation.say('the-carriers')` therefore returns null for her, structurally, every time. Not a hit-test bug, not a confirm-path bug: `_dialogueCtx()` was unconditionally drawing every AddTopic-named word regardless of whether THIS speaker could ever answer it, because an earlier fix (same day) deliberately removed the `infoFor` filter that used to gate this — for a real reason (it had collapsed link density to near zero project-wide) — but removed it from `st.topics` and `_dlgAdds` alike, when only the latter needed the removal.
defect_1.fix: `game/src/engine.js`, `Engine._dialogueCtx()`: `_dlgAdds` entries are now added to the drawn candidate set only if the CURRENT speaker can actually answer them — checked via the same two paths `Conversation.say()` itself uses (`infoFor()`, or the registered-mystery `opacity.refusalFor()` decline, which is itself a real spoken answer). `st.topics` (already filtered by `topicsFor()`) is untouched, so the prior fix's own measured win (87-97 lightable spans/speaker, not 0-7) is not regressed. The word still enters the player's PERMANENT vocabulary unconditionally — `learnTopics()` already runs the instant the ORIGINATING rumour is heard, before this filter runs — so nothing is lost on that promise; only THIS speaker stops making one she cannot keep.

evidence.pre_fix_capture_matches_gate_g: Visually and structurally identical to the judge's original capture (`quillon/shots5/012-022`): three presses on 'the carriers' produce three identical frames, blocks 2->2, lines 7->7, text unchanged.
evidence.post_fix: Neekhu no longer draws 'the-carriers' as a column row or a link at all (checked D1-2); `questTopicsKnown()` still includes 'the-carriers' (checked D1-3) — the permanent-index promise holds.

defect_2.name: Pressing the same phrase twice prints the paragraph twice
defect_2.diagnosis: NOT a second, distinct path into the same behaviour — established by reading `Engine._conversationStep()`: inline links and column rows both resolve through the identical unified route (`UISystem.dialogueStep()` -> `_dialogueConfirm()` -> `Engine._convPending` -> `conversationSay()`), with no branch specific to either. The morning's `_dlgSaySeq` fix is not incomplete on its own terms either — it correctly stopped 'any re-ask prints nothing', which is what it was built and verified to fix. The Gate G capture is the SAME mechanism doing exactly what it was built to do: 'the curfew' was, at the moment of the second press, the CURRENT LAST BLOCK in Sigurd's transcript (confirmed via `quillon/shots4/`'s own session log: the sequence between the two 'the curfew' presses is only a no-op 'down' at the clamped end of the link list, not a different topic) — i.e. the exact scenario the seq-fix intentionally changed FROM SILENT TO REPRINTED. 'Reprint' was the correct call against the (never-measured) prior assumption that Morrowind re-prints; Gate G is the first real human evidence on the question, and both judges independently called the verbatim duplicate 'the worst thing' in the build.
defect_2.fix: `game/src/ui/screens/dialogue.js`, `DialogueHistory.append()`: once the existing seq-gate (unchanged; still the guard against the SAME say-event being read 60x/second) confirms this is a genuinely new say, the method now searches the WHOLE transcript — not only the last block — for an existing block with the identical `(topic, text)`. If found, that block is moved to the end instead of a duplicate being pushed; if not, it is pushed exactly as before (so an ordinary, non-repeated answer is unchanged, and a re-ask of a DIFFERENT-from-current-last topic still visibly re-surfaces — this is a real, provable state change: the block's position and the transcript order change, even though duplicate text never appears). `game/src/ui/system.js` additionally resets scroll-to-bottom whenever a genuinely new say lands, so a re-ask made after scrolling up to reread earlier answers snaps the view back down (checked directly; see the residual above for the one case this does not yet fully cover).

evidence.pre_fix_capture_matches_gate_g: Byte-for-byte visual match to `quillon/shots4/025`: 'the curfew' appears twice, identical heading, identical 87-char body, back to back.
evidence.post_fix: 'the curfew' has exactly one block after the second confirm (checked D2-2); confirming a scrolled-away re-ask on a forced-overflow viewport snaps `scrolled_to_bottom` from false to true via the real KeyE press for topics that are NOT the current last block — the one narrow exception is the residual named above.

how_it_was_proved.real_input_only: Every reproduction and every confirmation of the fix is driven through actual `KeyboardEvent`/`MouseEvent`/`PointerEvent` dispatch at the page via `tools/ui/dialogue-gate-g-repro.mjs` (new; reuses `dialogue-drive-probe.mjs`'s proven shape and its I0 instrument check verbatim) — nothing calls `_convPending`, `dialogueFocus`, or `DialogueHistory.append()` directly. `A.talkTo()` and one direct `dialogueScroll` write are used ONLY as harness-door PRECONDITIONS (opening a conversation; simulating a player who had scrolled up), exactly the same pattern `dialogue-drive-probe.mjs` already uses for opening conversations — never for the confirm or scroll action actually under test.
how_it_was_proved.delete_the_fix_from_a_pinned_sha_not_HEA: Per the brief's explicit instruction, NOT `HEAD~1`. Baseline commit `6df8d003` (the tree immediately before either defect's fix landed) was verified free of my work by `git diff 6df8d003 139e23d9 --stat` and by grepping both changed files for my own comment markers (0 hits) before use. `game/` was extracted from that exact commit via `git archive 6df8d003 game | tar -x` into a disposable scratch directory (the repo's disk was at 96%/1.7GB free, so a full `git worktree add` of the whole tree — which also pulls multi-GB `docs/shots/` — failed with ENOSPC; `git archive` of just `game/` avoided that entirely, 36 MB). `dialogue-gate-g-repro.mjs` gained an `--entry` flag to serve that pinned checkout instead of the live tree. Result: 7/7 checks pass against the pinned baseline, reproducing BOTH defects again, byte-for-byte identical to the original pre-fix run — proving the fix, not the environment, is what changed.
how_it_was_proved.full_regression_suite: `tools/ui/dialogue-drive-probe.mjs` (the existing, pre-owned comprehensive probe) run in full before and after: IDENTICAL 15/18 pass pattern both times, with the identical three pre-existing failures (K4's Persuasion-only dead row, K5/M2's 0-links-at-this-NPC content gap) in both runs — zero new failures from either fix. Getting to that identical result required fixing a real methodology gap in K4 itself: its fixed-index walk was contaminated by K3 having already answered row 1 moments earlier (an artifact, not a player action), and its 'lines increased' success criterion no longer distinguishes a legitimate de-duplicated re-ask (which correctly does not add lines) from a truly dead control. Fixed by reopening on a fresh transcript before the K4 walk and by treating a changed TAIL block (not just added lines) as evidence the confirm did something — documented in the file itself.
how_it_was_proved.reports_directory: reports/uix08/gate-g-repro/, reports/uix08/gate-g-repro-deletefix/, reports/uix08/p1-regression-before/, reports/uix08/p1-regression-after5/ — left on disk but NOT committed, because `reports/.gitignore` excludes every `*.json`/`*.png` in `reports/` by default (HAZARDS.md §9's exact warning: evidence under `reports/` can silently never reach the remote). The cited copies actually tracked and pushed live at `corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/P1-DIALOGUE-DEFECTS/`, the route HAZARDS §9 names as the one other verdicts already use — 7 JSON reports + 7 representative screenshots, 7.3 MB total.
